sections.h2: Where a Columbiana County deed is filed
sections.html:
The Columbiana County Recorder files deeds at the courthouse in Lisbon, phone 330-424-9517. Section 5301.25 puts a deed on the record of the county where the land sits. An unrecorded deed is treated as fraudulent against a later buyer who knew nothing about it. Recording is therefore the closing step of your sale.

Beyond deeds, the office handles mortgages, easements and military discharge papers. A new filing is recorded and can be searched right away. After quality control, staff return the originals to whoever submitted them. You can also order copies of plats and old maps, from 8 by 11 up to 36 by 80, at $2 to $5 each depending on the paper.

Costs come from three places: the recorder, the auditor and, if one exists, the county transfer tax. Every state recording charge is split evenly between the recorder and the Ohio Housing Trust Fund. A county can add its own preservation surcharge of up to $5, and the amount varies. Call the office for the Columbiana County number before closing day.

ChargeStatutory amount
Deed filing, pages one and two (section 317.32)$17 to the recorder plus $17 to the housing trust fund
Every further page (section 317.32)$4 to the recorder plus $4 to the housing trust fund
Preservation surcharge (section 317.32)Up to $5, county decides
Auditor's conveyance fee (section 319.54)$1 or 10 cents per $100 of value, whichever is more
Auditor's entry fee (section 319.54)50 cents per transfer
County transfer tax, if levied (section 322.02)Capped at 30 cents per $100 of value

Ask the Columbiana County Auditor whether the commissioners levy the county transfer tax. The figure above is a statutory ceiling, so it may not apply here.

Ahead of the recorder, the auditor transfers the parcel to the buyer on the tax list and endorses the deed. Section 319.202 puts the value statement on the buyer and the conveyance fee on the seller. Any mortgage balance staying with the property counts toward value.

Two questions on the form fit a county of town lots and farms. Did the property get an owner-occupancy or homestead tax reduction? Was the land in the agricultural use valuation program, and how will a recoupment charge be handled if it leaves? Sellers of acreage in the northern townships should expect that second question.

Some transfers owe no conveyance fee. Common ones:

  • A gift between spouses, or from a parent to a child
  • A division among heirs where no money changes hands
  • A corrective deed repairing an earlier deed
  • A trust's maker moving property into or out of a revocable trust

Put the exemption reason on the value statement, and settle on the wording before you go to the auditor in Lisbon. If you are unsure which exemption fits a family transfer, the auditor's office can tell you before you sign, which is cheaper than refiling a deed that was marked wrong.

The seller signs the deed and acknowledges it before an official listed in section 5301.01: a judge, court clerk, county auditor, county engineer, notary or mayor. Your bank or title company probably has a notary. Section 319.20 has the auditor look for three more things:

  • A mailing address for at least one buyer
  • The volume and page, or other marker, of the seller's own deed
  • A legal description that lines up with the tax list

When only part of a parcel changes hands, the auditor divides the tax value between the piece sold and the piece kept. Any back taxes on the original parcel are then shared out by value if the buyer or the remaining owner asks.

sections.h2: How recording works from start to finish
sections.html: The title agent or an attorney prepares the deed, and you sign before a notary. The deed and the completed value statement go to the auditor, who checks the legal description against the tax list, takes the conveyance fee and endorses the deed. From there it moves to the recorder, who charges the filing fee for the pages and any preservation surcharge, then records it. The record is searchable right away, and the original returns to whoever submitted it. If an old loan is being paid off, its release is recorded separately, so confirm with the lender that it has been sent. Keeping these steps in order avoids a bounced deed and a delayed closing. Ask the auditor and the recorder at the counter how each wants its payment handed in, and bring a second form of payment in case one office refuses a check.

The county sits along Ohio's eastern border. Pennsylvania lies to the east, Mahoning County to the north, and the Ohio River runs about 20 miles along the south. Its 534 square miles hold 18 townships. Level, fertile farmland covers the north, while the south is hilly, with limestone soils that suit pasture, orchards and timber. After Salem, the largest cities are East Liverpool and Columbiana.

The July 2025 population estimate is 99,377, which is 2.5% under the April 2020 base. Counted housing units total 46,220 and households 41,459, with 72.7% of homes owner-occupied. Median home value is $151,600, median monthly rent is $756 and median household income is $58,180. A house on a village street in Lisbon and a farmhouse in Madison Township will sit far apart, so use a written offer or local appraisal for the real number on your own property.

sections.h2: Preparing before you go to Lisbon
sections.html:
Each item here takes about one phone call, and doing them a few days ahead keeps the closing on schedule:

  • Get the amount owed on the parcel from the county treasurer, so the title company can pay it from the proceeds
  • Have any lender record the release of an old mortgage
  • If the owner has died, ask the probate court which papers allow a sale and who signs
  • Match the legal description on your deed to the tax record
  • Agree on who covers any farm-use recoupment or open assessment

The same route applies when a house is sold as-is for cash. The deed still passes through the auditor first and the recorder second. Salem, East Liverpool, Columbiana and the villages all file in the same Lisbon office, so a seller in Wellsville or Leetonia does not need a separate local filing. Bring the signed deed, the completed value statement and a way to pay each office, and ask at the counter how the recorder and the auditor want the payments handed in.

faqs.q: Can I reach the Columbiana County Recorder by phone?
faqs.a: Yes, at 330-424-9517. The office is at the courthouse in Lisbon.

faqs.q: What is the preservation surcharge on a deed filed in Columbiana County?
faqs.a: State law lets a county charge up to $5 per document, and the amount varies by county. Ask the office for the current Columbiana County charge.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller pay the conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The seller pays it under section 319.202, while the buyer files the statement of value. If the county levies a transfer tax, the seller pays that as well.

faqs.q: Can relatives transfer a house without the conveyance fee?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Section 319.54 exempts gifts between spouses or between a parent and child, and splits among heirs when no money is paid. The reason must be stated on the value statement.

faqs.q: What if the deed is signed but never filed?
faqs.a: The deed is still a signed document, but section 5301.25 treats it as fraudulent against a later purchaser with no knowledge of it. Filing with the recorder closes that gap.
